newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed in busy trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed in busy trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed in busy markets dominated by uncertainty over an impending U.S. announcement on whether it would reinstate Colombia to its list of allies in the drug war, after being blacklisted last March.

Bogota's IBB index dipped 0.08 percent to 1,032.02 amid a 3 billion peso volume while Medellin's IBOMED general price index edged up marginally 0.05 percent to 16,190.19 amid a 1.95 billion peso volume.
"The market showed no real trend because of uncertainty over the effects of possible decertification and the likely drop in interest rates. There were lots of ups and downs," said one Bogota broker.

The United States is due to announce on Feb 27 whether it will "certify" Colombia next week or leave it on a list of virtual pariah states which it considers are not doing enough to stem drug trafficking. The United States decertified Colombia in March last year. It is not clear whether a similar decision this year would be accompanied by economic sanctions.
Cement manufacturer Cementos Caribe, part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial group, gained 3.61 percent to close at 5,700 in Bogota but dropped 2.31 percent to 5,500 in Medellin.
Cemento Argos, the flagship cement company in Sindicato Antioqueno, rose 0.41 percent to 7,230 in Bogota and 0.42 percent in Medellin, where it also closed at 7,230.
The IBB index was pushed down by falls in Banco Ganadero ordinary shares, down 0.63 percent to 314 and in Bavaria, down 0.4 percent to 6,673.
In Medellin, Banco de Colombia dropped 0.01 percent to 420.
